comments: Hydrostatic damping of heave, roll and pitch for sail::DampingModule: generalised force -(b_lin*qdot + b_quad*|qdot|*qdot) per DOF, with qdot measured against the water surface: heave is the CG's world-vertical velocity and its force is along world z, roll and pitch are the world angular velocity about the horizontal heading axis and the horizontal axis to port of it, and their moments are about those axes. Body-frame rates are not used because steady forward motion at a trim angle, or heeled with leeway, has a body-z velocity, and a heeled turn has a body pitch rate r*sin(heel), neither of which any hydrostatic stiffness resists. Every coefficient is a fraction of critical damping and the absolute values are derived at load time from the current mass and added mass, so this file stays valid when mass or hull change. The stiffnesses are the measurement-trim certificate values in every mass configuration, so with crew aboard, whose height changes the roll and pitch stiffness, the realised damping ratios depart from nominal by the square root of that stiffness change. Critical damping per DOF: b_crit = 2*sqrt(k*(M + A)), with M + A the rigid-body mass or inertia plus the added mass of that DOF from the mass model. Linear: b_lin = zeta_linear*b_crit. Quadratic: b_quad = zeta_quadratic*b_crit/reference_velocity, so at qdot = reference_velocity the quadratic force equals the linear force of a damper of ratio zeta_quadratic. Heave stiffness: k = rho*g*A_wp, with A_wp = sink*1000/rho from the certificate immersion (particulars.json sink, 8.99 kg/mm), M + A = mass + heave added mass. Roll stiffness: k = Delta*g*GM with GM = RM/(Delta*g*sin(1 deg)), which is k = RM/sin(1 deg) with the certificate measured RM at 1 deg (particulars.json righting_moment_1deg, 264.8 N*m); M + A = Ixx + roll added mass. The morphed hull_physics.obj is about 13% stiffer in roll than the certificate (see particulars.json vcgm); the certificate value is used because the certificate is the measurement and this keeps the module independent of the mesh, which makes the real roll damping ratio about 6% (sqrt(1.13)) below nominal in the simulation, well inside the uncertainty of the zeta values. Pitch stiffness: k = Delta*g*GM_L with GM_L = I_L/V, the waterplane longitudinal inertia over the displaced volume (KB - KG is under 2% of GM_L and is neglected), so k = rho*g*I_L. The dossier has no measured I_L, so it is estimated from hull_hydro.json result values as I_L = Cw^2*BWL*LWL^3/12, which equals the rectangle value B*L^3/12 scaled by Cw^2, the usual fine-waterplane approximation; M + A = Iyy + pitch added mass. A DampingModule multiplier per DOF scales both linear and quadratic coefficients for heavy-damped settling. Roll and the keel and rudder foil modules: those modules take the full angular velocity at each foil, so they damp roll themselves, by lift in proportion to forward speed and by cross-flow drag at any speed (they add no pitch damping, since pitch rate moves a vertical foil only along its chord and span). At 3 m/s and measurement trim the keel adds 3398 N*m*s/rad, zeta 0.24 of the roll b_crit 13962, and the rudder 77 (zeta 0.006), against the lumped linear 977 (zeta 0.07); at rest they add no linear term. The lumped roll terms are therefore kept as the hull-and-zero-speed share: zeta_linear stays the zero-speed value, which no foil term duplicates, and zeta_quadratic loses the foils' measured cross-flow share. In the simulation (gravity, hydrostatics, this module, hull forces, keel and rudder, from 5 deg heel) roll decay gives zeta about 0.10 at rest and 0.15 at 3 m/s: the free decay at speed is well under the 0.31 the coefficients add up to, since the keel's side force couples roll into sway and yaw, which that sum ignores.

zeta_linear.source: estimate for a displacement keelboat; no measurement for the J/80
zeta_linear.method: heave and pitch of a keelboat radiate wave energy and sit around 0.1-0.2 of critical; mid-range taken

zeta_quadratic.source: estimate for a displacement keelboat; no measurement for the J/80
zeta_quadratic.method: viscous drag on the keel, rudder and hull bottom grows with speed; at the reference velocity it adds two thirds of the linear damping

reference_velocity.method: typical heave velocity of the boat in a short chop

zeta_linear.source: estimate for a keelboat; no measurement for the J/80
zeta_linear.method: zero-speed roll damping of a keelboat without bilge keels, wave making and eddy making, 0.05-0.1 of critical; mid-range taken. The keel and rudder foil modules add no linear roll damping at rest, and their lift damping grows with forward speed, so this is not reduced for them

zeta_quadratic.source: estimate for a keelboat; no measurement for the J/80
zeta_quadratic.method: cross-flow drag of the keel, rudder and hull bottom dominates at large roll rates; estimated at 0.1, less the 0.019 the keel and rudder foil modules carry as their own cross-flow drag at rest and the reference velocity (134 N*m of 698 N*m at measurement trim)

reference_velocity.method: about 29 deg/s, a brisk roll rate in a gust

zeta_linear.source: estimate for a displacement keelboat; no measurement for the J/80
zeta_linear.method: heave and pitch of a keelboat sit around 0.1-0.2 of critical; mid-range taken

zeta_quadratic.source: estimate for a displacement keelboat; no measurement for the J/80
zeta_quadratic.method: viscous drag on the keel, rudder and hull ends grows with speed

reference_velocity.method: about 17 deg/s, a typical pitch rate in a short chop
